claims.text: High-energy ball milling followed by rapid, low-temperature sintering will suppress porosity in CoCrFeNiTi.
The proposed route will kinetically trap a nanocrystalline FCC solid solution.
The processed alloy will contain a minor BCC phase in addition to dominant FCC.
Rapid solid-state processing will bypass brittle HCP formation associated with Ti-rich segregation.
The effective processing regime is 800–900°C, a heating rate above 100°C/min, and a dwell below 10 minutes.
Maintaining the sintering strain rate below 10^-3 s^-1 will prevent excessive grain growth.
High-energy milling introduces severe lattice distortion and a high dislocation density.
Milling-induced defects lower the activation energy for FCC nucleation.
Milling-induced defects increase the kinetic barrier for formation of a slower-diffusing Ti-rich HCP phase.
Rapid sintering uses stored mechanical energy from milling to drive densification.
Limiting thermal exposure prevents the HCP phase from nucleating and growing.
Rapid solidification increases nucleation and promotes grain refinement.
Rapid solidification or grain refinement promotes FCC phase stability.
The proposed process will produce density above 99% of theoretical density.
The proposed process will produce a grain size below 100 nm.
The processed alloy will have less than 2 vol% HCP phase.
The processed alloy will exhibit Vickers hardness above 500 HV.
Conventionally cast CoCrFeNiTi has more than 10 vol% brittle HCP phase, which leads to hardness below 350 HV and poor ductility.
Temperatures above 950°C or dwell times above 30 minutes allow Ti-rich HCP to nucleate and grow.
A lack of hardness increase at 0.1 mN relative to 10 mN would distinguish solute strengthening from grain-refinement strengthening.

contradictions.description: The structural mediator states that the HCP nucleation barrier is suppressed, which ordinarily means reduced, whereas the mechanism says milling increases the kinetic barrier to HCP formation.
The hypothesis specifies sintering below 900°C, while the stated operating interval includes 900°C.
